About

Hi, I'm Harith.

Updated Oct 7, 2026

My first computer was my dad's old laptop with 500 MB of RAM.

I'm a founder and tech nerd from Kuala Lumpur. These days I run DagangNow, an agentic commerce platform for Malaysian sellers. Before that I was the camera guy at uni, and before that I was a kid trying to get YouTube to load on a laptop that had no business running it.

Where it started

I was fifteen and my parents were strict, so no phone. What I did have was access to my dad's old gear, and he had a lot of it. One piece was an old VAIO with 500 MB of RAM. I wanted the internet badly, mostly for YouTube and games, so I had to get creative.

I learned how to install Linux. I borrowed my cousin's CD drive, burned distros onto CDs and kept trying until one of them worked. I wouldn't call it hacking. It was modding an old machine back to life so I could use it, and it's how I got into tech at all.

Games pulled me further in. I'd rip open compact HP office desktops and try to fit graphics cards inside so they could pass as gaming PCs. Once I had a bit of money, it went into microphones and audio gear. I've always liked the small, gritty details of how things work.

Uni, and the camera

At UTM I couldn't decide between electrical and software engineering, so I took the tech foundation first. I picked software engineering because I wanted to be able to work remotely, and figured I could teach myself the electrical side. I'll be honest: for the first couple of years I wasn't paying much attention.

Then, in my second year, I got obsessed with photography. My mentor, Fika Azman, is a professional photographer, and I nerded out about cameras the same way I had about computers. I started a club, SSC UTMKL (the Sakura Sakura Club), and became the go-to cameraman. People knew me as the camera guy and came to me for studio shoots.

That same year a lecturer wanted to build a studio and brought me in. I was the first person to help. I had no experience, just a lot of hunger to learn. For over a year I shot studio, outdoor, cosplay and product work, ran one-on-one sessions, and held studio sessions for juniors. I'm still digging those photos up for the gallery.

Back to tech

In third year I decided it was time to change. I started joining hackathons and lost a lot of them, because I didn't really know how to code yet. Building apps for them is what got me learning Next.js, and I've been diving into tech ever since.

My internship at Asterisk Digital is where I went properly deep. I was put on a mobile team using React Native and Expo, and I loved going into the libraries: Zustand, React Hook Form, state management and how it all fits together.

I moved across projects after that. I built a mobile app and then a prototype, set up EC2 instances and cloud infrastructure on AWS, and was then placed with a gas-company client as a full-stack engineer doing mostly data engineering: QuickSight, Glue jobs, PySpark and a lot of SQL. While I was there, I helped build and prototype an AI tool for the whole department.

Now

Now I'm building my own thing. DagangNow is an agentic commerce platform for Malaysian SMEs. Sellers who live on Shopee, TikTok and WhatsApp get a store of their own, with an AI WhatsApp assistant, a catalogue AI agents can read, and orders, shipping and affiliates in one place. The tagline says it best: your AI-powered eCommerce store, live in minutes.

I still lift. My bench is at 70 kg and I'd like that number to keep going up. The A7R III still comes with me most places. And I still can't leave a piece of hardware alone if it has screws in it.

Still tinkering.
